title: Tool Calling Is Not Just Plumbing for AI Agents — Roy Derks
talk_summary: Roy Derks argues that tool calling is the fragile part of agents and should be treated as reusable, separately hosted infrastructure rather than code embedded in each agent framework. He covers MCP/tool platforms, output schemas, centralized auth/errors/chaining, and dynamic schema-based tools to avoid huge static tool lists.

takeaways.technique: Separate tools from agent framework via MCP/tool server
takeaways.what_they_do: Define reusable tools in a standalone MCP/tool server and let agents import/execute them remotely, so tool logic is not duplicated inside each agent framework.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the mCP server is where you handle the logic you define your tools import your tools

takeaways.technique: Central tool execution for auth, retries, and chaining
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a tool platform/server to own credentials, authorization, error handling, retries, and chained tool calls instead of embedding that logic in each agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is also where you can handle authorization and errors and these kind of things

takeaways.what_they_do: Add output schemas to tool definitions so models know the returned data shape and can chain calls with structured outputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you don't have an output schema how's the model going to know what data is being returned

takeaways.technique: Dynamic schema-based tools instead of many static tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose a schema/query language and let the model generate a query, reducing dozens of CRUD tools and duplicated business logic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're going to paste in a 100 tools to the agent it's get really confused

takeaways.technique: Treat tool descriptions as system prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Write simple tool names and detailed descriptions with usage rules, examples, and failure modes, because the description steers model tool selection.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this to me almost feels like a system prompt for the large language model

takeaways.technique: Keep explicit control over the tool-call loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Prefer traditional/explicit tool calling over embedded black-box agent executors so retries, errors, and tool decisions are visible and controllable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't have any control over the tool calling process
